title.narrative: Strategy to advance pilot projects for public transport service improvement in Cusco is elaborated

comment.narrative: The SUMP activity has been delayed for an extended period of time due to disagreements between the previous administrations of both Cusco Provincial Municipality (CPM) and Cusco Regional Government (CRG). The CPM and CRG signed the delegation agreement, allowing for the implementation of this activity. The strategy to advance pilot projects in public transport service improvement is included in the SUMP contract under Component 2. The SUMP Contract was signed in August 2024 and the first deliverable (work plan and methodology) was accepted by the supervision team before Project closing. This indicator did not achieve its target at the closing date.

title.narrative: 1. Average travel time savings in the east-west corridor of Cusco Provincial Municipality (San Jeronimo District – Cusco District)

comment.narrative: According to the measurements by the PIU, it now takes 11.5 minutes downhill (west to east) and 15.5 minutes uphill (east to west) by car during the morning peak time. Baseline travel times were estimated as 22 minutes downhill (west to east) and 28 minutes (east to west), resulting in savings of 10.54 minutes and 12.50 minutes, respectively. Thus, the average time savings exceed the target of 10 minutes

title.narrative: 2. Change in accessibility to employment opportunities by public transport in the area of influence of the east-west corridor of Cusco Provincial Municipality (San Jeronimo District – Cusco District)

comment.narrative: The project achieved 18.8 percent in ‘Change in accessibility to employment opportunities by public transport in the area of influence of the east-west corridor of CPM (San Jeronimo District - Cusco District) (Percentage)’, exceeding the target of 15 percent. Based on the current bus operation on the Via Expresa Avenue, the project has enabled access to an additional 40,800 jobs by public transport within 30 minutes of commuting. It is expected that this accessibility will further increase as bus operations on the Via Expresa Avenue intensify after the bus route optimization next year

title.narrative: 3. User satisfaction with Via Expresa Avenue

comment.narrative: Based on a sample of 578 users of the Via Expresa, approximately 54 percent were overall satisfied with the project, falling short of the 70 percent target, while 27 percent remained neutral. Safety concerns regarding road signage and traffic signs were cited by 19 percent who were dissatisfied. However, the majority of the respondents appreciate reduced travel times (76 percent), improved connectivity, bike lanes, and public transport stops that promote sustainable transportation. The project has also shown potential for a shift from private vehicles to public transport, cycling, and walking, as evidenced by high pedestrian and cyclist activity on opening day. The corridor's design, which includes amenities such as mini gyms, walkways, and cycling tracks, further supports non-motorized transport (NMT).

As at 15 December 2024, all the civil works under component 1 were completed. The new infrastructure features eight lanes, four bridges, and 42 public transport stops, 6.35km of cycling length, 8 play playgrounds for children, 13km of tactile sidewalks, 9 mini public gyms, 62 concrete benches, 19 drinking fountains 112 trash cans and 8 security booths

Physical progress of Component 1 stands at 86% by the end of June 2024, estimated to be at 94% at the end of August. Remaining works include some pavement, signs and markings, green area and landscaping, electrical installations and traffic lights, will be carried out by the client using counterpart funds. Expected completion is the end of October 2024.

title.narrative: 4. Design and execution of Via Expresa Avenue works are informed with at least three audits and/or road safety inspections

comment.narrative: One road safety audit was conducted during the design (Expediente Tecnico) of Via Expresa Avenue civil works. Another road safety audit was concluded in August 2024 on the final design and identified corrective measures will be partially incorporated into the final construction, to be completed by October 2024. The post-construction road safety inspection was conducted in February 2025 and report completed in March 1, 2025.
